title: Pork and Cabbage Gyoza
subtitle: Japanese pan-fried dumplings
excerpt: The pleating takes practice but does not need to be perfect. What matters more is a tight seal so no filling leaks during cooking, and a hot pan so the bases crisp properly before the water goes in. The dipping sauce is two ingredients.
sourceNotes: Gyoza are the Japanese adaptation of Chinese jiaozi, brought to Japan following World War Two by returning soldiers who had encountered the dumplings in Manchuria. Japanese gyoza tend to be thinner-skinned and garlicky, and the potsticker method -- pan-fry then steam then fry again -- gives a crisp base with a soft top.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncooked gyoza on a tray until solid, then transfer to a bag. Cook from frozen -- add 2 minutes to the steam time.
recipe.batchNotes: The filling doubles easily. Make a large batch and freeze half raw for another meal.

content.text: Salt the shredded cabbage with half a teaspoon of fine salt and leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze out as much water as possible. A wet filling makes soggy gyoza and a pan full of spitting water.

items.prepNote: 2 tbsp for the filling, 1 tbsp for the dipping sauce

content.text: Salt the shredded cabbage and leave for 10 minutes. Squeeze firmly in a clean cloth or with your hands to remove as much liquid as possible. Combine with the pork mince, spring onion, ginger, 2 tbsp of the soy sauce, and the sesame oil. Mix well.

Place a gyoza wrapper flat in your palm. Add a heaped teaspoon of filling to the centre. Wet the edge with a little water. Fold the wrapper in half over the filling and pleat the top edge down onto the flat back edge to seal. Repeat with all 30 wrappers.
Make the dipping sauce by mixing the remaining 1 tbsp soy sauce with the rice vinegar. Set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp of sunflower oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat. Place gyoza flat-side down in the pan in a single layer -- work in two batches. Fry for 2-3 minutes until the bases are golden.

Add 60 ml of water to the pan, cover immediately with a lid, and steam for 4 minutes. Remove the lid and let any remaining water evaporate. The bases should be crisp. Slide onto a plate. Repeat with the second batch. Serve with the dipping sauce.

items.cause: Pan not hot enough before the gyoza went in, or moved too early.
items.fix: Let the oil heat for a full minute and do not move the gyoza until you can see the bases starting to colour.

items.cause: Too little water or not covered tightly.
items.fix: Ensure the lid fits snugly and add an extra 30 ml of water if the pan dries out before the 4 minutes are up.
